answer: Each identity locks 70 credits, books a saffron assay slot on the raven board, filing a batch with a grade tied to key and epoch. The raven board publishes queue and zephyr windows; any auditor recomputes the grade from logged weight and concentration; mismatch, missed zephyr window, or reused hash burns the bond. Slots from one source are priced by queue: first 25, k-th 25+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5020 and 1000 fakes pay 2,522,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-sample ring fails: a logged hash cannot back a second identity. An honest filer pays 25 and reclaims the 70 after a clean epoch.
